examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of a Triangle
examples.problem:
Find the area of the triangle $\triangle ABC.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945897/assets/f892cd084f548769fa6b7352fece0e1aef3a66a4ab517ed5b5243d89041ac3a9.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac{b \cdot h}{2},
$$

 

where $b$ is a base and $h$ is the corresponding height.

From the diagram, we see that the base is

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =AB \\  & =AH+HB \\  & =6+3 \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

and the corresponding height is

$$
h={CH} = 4 .
$$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{b\cdot h}{2} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 4}{2} \\  & =\frac{36}{2} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
